title: Diagnose and recover scoped PostgreSQL lock contention
trigger: A transaction-dependent customer update is hanging or timing out while PostgreSQL remains reachable and telemetry indicates lock waiting rather than a database-wide outage.
preconditions: confirm PostgreSQL is reachable and this is not a database-wide outage
capture the affected customer/query scope and first observed timestamp
identify the waiting backend and its wait_event_type before considering termination
use pg_blocking_pids and pg_locks to prove the exact blocker relationship
capture blocker PID, application_name, transaction age, query text, and ownership context
confirm the proposed recovery is permitted by the current incident runbook or approval path
diagnostic_steps: query pg_stat_activity for waiting sessions, transaction age, wait_event_type, wait_event, and query text
use pg_blocking_pids(waiter_pid) to identify blocking backend IDs
join blocker IDs back to pg_stat_activity to capture application_name and query context
inspect pg_locks for granted and waiting lock rows
check whether the blocker is part of an expected deployment, migration, maintenance job, or business transaction
check for broader connection saturation or multiple unrelated blockers before classifying the incident as scoped
mitigation_steps: do not restart PostgreSQL to resolve a single proven blocker
do not terminate arbitrary backends based only on age or lock count
if the exact blocker is proven, tagged as the approved simulated exercise session, and recovery is authorized, terminate only that backend
if blocker ownership, business safety, replication impact, or transaction criticality is unclear, escalate to DBA/application ownership instead of terminating it
validation_steps: waiting session exits the Lock wait state
affected transaction completes or fails in a controlled and understood way
expected customer state is visible after recovery
no DB-002 exercise blocker/waiter sessions remain
PostgreSQL remains reachable without a service restart
incident evidence includes the blocker/waiter mapping captured before recovery
escalation_boundary: Escalate to DBA/application ownership if the blocker is not the explicitly approved simulated session, if multiple production transactions are involved, if termination could lose important work, if the blocker immediately recurs, or if lock contention is caused by application transaction design requiring code or schema changes.
